summary: Local health organizations launched the "Step Up Your Game" public health campaign on September 5, 2023 to counter sedentary lifestyles linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart disease and early mortality. The note covers the science of exercise, community initiatives, barriers such as cost and time, education efforts, school pilot programs and employer wellness programs. The campaign plans to expand indoor activities as winter approaches.
one_line: The "Step Up Your Game" campaign, launched September 5, 2023, promotes exercise through community events, education, school programs and workplace wellness to combat sedentary lifestyles.
key_facts: The "Step Up Your Game" campaign began on September 5, 2023, led by local health organizations to promote exercise and physical activity.
A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and early mortality.
Dr. Lisa Greene, a public health expert, called increased sedentary behavior a global health crisis and said inactivity "is like a slow poison to our body."
Dr. Greene spoke on September 10, 2023, at the campaign's first community workshop.
Physical inactivity can lead to metabolic syndrome, poor mental health, and a reduction in skeletal muscle mass.
Exercise improves muscle fibers' ability to metabolize sugar and fat, and endorphins released during exercise can reduce depression, anxiety, and stress.
Initiatives include "Walk and Talk" meetings and "Cycle to Work" days; gym owner John Michaels has hosted free weekend workout sessions since September 15, 2023.
A survey distributed in early October found cost, lack of time, and a dearth of local amenities were the top three barriers to regular physical activity.
The campaign introduced an online platform with free at-home workout videos ranging from low-impact exercises to high-intensity training.
Nutritionist Emily White began a series of webinars on October 12 about how diet and exercise amplify each other's benefits.
School pilot programs launched in several local schools on October 20, using gamification, mandatory activity breaks, adjusted PE curriculums and after-school sports clubs.
Darren Fletcher, a high school PE teacher, wants exercise to be a norm "just like brushing their teeth."
Employer wellness programs, some starting as soon as November 1, include subsidized gym memberships, onsite yoga classes, and wellness workshops.
As winter approaches, the campaign plans to expand indoor activities and support systems to maintain momentum.
